content.text: USU B. pertussis (gram - coccobacillus) - may be other Bordetella spp
MC summer & fall - morbidity & mortality highest <1y
•coughing · sneezing · sharing breathing space for extended periods
DTaP infants & young children · Tdap older children & adults · Td booster
vax ↓risk & severity - prevention: vax + avoid others w pertussis sxs
: URI sxs lasting 1-2wks (rhinorrhea, low-grade fevers, sneezing) · poor feeding/sleeping
•like mild URI: cough · watery coryza · nasal congestion
severe paroxysmal coughing fits w inspir whooping sound after cough fits
•long series of coughs w little to no inspiration - may gag · cyanosis · appear to struggle to breathe
•whoop = forceful inspiration after prolonged coughing bout - spontaneous or ← external stimuli - dyspnea · gagging · cyanosis · diaphoresis · post-tussive emesis - worse at night
may present w apnea or cyanosis & often
•post-tussive vomiting more common in infants <1y than older children
: MC PNA · wt loss ← feeding difficulties & vomiting · apnea
paroxysms of coughing, inspir whoop, post-tussive emesis, apnea in infants <1y
•high suspicion early to test & start mgnt - recent contact w lab-confirmed case ↑likelihood
•<3mo, favors pertussis over viral resp dz: paroxysmal cough · post-tussive emesis · Sx >10d · ⍉fever · ⍉congestion · cyanosis · apnea · sz · leukocytosis ← lymphocytosis
•lab testing confirms - PCR & cx of nasopharyngeal specimen = most appropriate & common - polyethylene terephthalate swab if both PCR & cx ordered
•nasopharyngeal (⍉oropharyngeal) specimen - B. pertussis primarily in resp secretions
•PCR on nasopharyngeal specimen preferred 1st 3wks of illness (≥4mo) - sensitivity ↓ after 3wks → serology preferred
lab confirmation (cx or PCR) often used esp for contact tracing
prev vaccinated & ≥1y since last vax: serology IgG to PT
•serology only if ≥4mo & ⍉pertussis vax in past yr - serum = preferred specimen for most Ab testing
•serum: liquid after centrifuging clotted blood (⍉clotting factors) - plasma: liquid after centrifuging anticoagulated blood
: leukocytosis w WBC >15,000 w absolute lymphocytosis
•focus on hydration & nutritional status - early mgnt & supportive tx critical (may decline rapidly)
•infant <1mo w projectile vomiting w.in 1mo of macrolide → consider infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis
•⍉delay tx - lab confirmation can take up to 1wk
•TMP-SMX x14d = 2nd-line - for >2mo who can't tolerate macrolides
•indications: (+) cx/PCR w.in 6wks of cough onset if <1y or w.in 3wks if >1y · clinical dx w cough <21d
: infants <4mo (↑risk comp & rapid deterioration) · resp distress · inability to feed · cyanosis · apnea · sz · PNA
: droplet precautions until 5d of effective abx - or 21d since Sx onset if ⍉abx
: all household & close contacts · exposed pts at high risk for comp - most effective w.in 21d of index pt's cough onset
: complicated by apnea in 2/3 of pts · superinfection w other bact PNA · sz · encephalopathy · pulm HTN & death (particularly in infants <2mo)
